US Diverts Somali Migrants — Some With No Criminal Record — to Guantánamo's Former Terror Wing

At least eight Somali men, several with pending asylum claims or valid work permits and no criminal history, have been quietly diverted from routine ICE custody into Camp 6 — the wing built two decades ago to hold terrorism suspects — at Guantánamo Bay, with as many as twelve cycling through since the Trump administration's “Operation Metro Surge” crackdown began. Among them is Adam Abdullah, a 31-year-old St. Paul auto mechanic and documented asylum seeker arrested in December 2025, who says he was told he was being deported to Somalia and instead was shackled at the wrists and ankles and flown to Cuba. The administration points to a 2025 executive order expanding Guantánamo's migrant operation center to house up to 30,000 people and insists it holds only “the worst of the worst,” yet has produced no evidence of wrongdoing against Abdullah or several others. The ACLU, Human Rights Watch, and Minnesota Senator Tina Smith have all condemned the transfers as lawless, and detainee Hassan Abdi Abtidoon put it starkly: “I never expected to be arrested in a prison established for the terrorists who I fled from.”

Three wild dogs complete a 2,500-mile odyssey across Zambia

Three male African wild dogs, dubbed the Mayukuyuku males, trekked more than 2,560 miles across Zambia between mid-2025 and April 2026, the longest journey ever recorded for an African mammal, according to a study published in the journal Ecology. Researchers say the findings show protected areas “can't be islands” and underscore the need for wildlife corridors linking ecosystems across borders.
